definition: The Future of Truth: How AI Reshapes Reality is a 2026 book by American filmmaker and author Steven Rosenbaum about how artificial intelligence affects the concept of truth.
details: It was published by Matt Holt Books on May 12, 2026, to positive media attention; on May 19, in response to an inquiry from The New York Times, Rosenbaum acknowledged that the book itself contains multiple misattributed or false quotes that were hallucinated by AIs.

explainer.lead: Steven Rosenbaum's 2026 book on how AI reshapes the concept of truth, published to positive media attention. It matters as a case study because Rosenbaum acknowledged, after a New York Times inquiry, that the book itself contained multiple misattributed or false quotes hallucinated by AIs.

tiers.eli5: A book warning that computers make things up — which turned out to contain made-up quotes the author got from a computer.
tiers.practitioner: The lesson for engineers is that AI-generated quotations must be verified against primary sources before publication; the pitfall is trusting fluent output precisely on the topic of trust.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition or formula; the work is an argument about AI and truth. Its documented limitation is empirical: the published text contains multiple misattributed or false quotes hallucinated by AIs, acknowledged by the author on May 19, 2026.

explainer.example: A quote attributed to a real person in the book was not actually said by them; the attribution came from an AI hallucination.
